instance_recommendations.rationale: Best price-performance option. Same 4 vCPU / 16 GB spec as current m4.xlarge but on AMD EPYC 3rd-gen with improved IPC. Saves ~13.8% per instance, which at an average fleet size of ~82 instances translates to roughly $1,940/month savings. Drop-in replacement for Celery worker workloads.
Very close in cost to m6a.xlarge and also AMD-based. A solid fallback if m6a capacity is constrained in your AZ. Savings of ~13.7% per instance with equivalent specs.
Current baseline instance type. No migration risk but highest cost among recommended options. Retained as reference.

Latest Intel generation with highest single-thread performance. Marginal cost increase (~0.5%) but improved per-core throughput could reduce per-task latency and potentially allow running fewer instances. Consider if workload is CPU-bound per task.

rationale.scaling_policy: The current policy uses extremely low thresholds (0-2000 messages) which are mismatched with observed queue depths that average over 2 million messages and peak at ~17.6 million. The new steps are calibrated to the actual data distribution: (1) 0-500 messages: queue is essentially drained, aggressively scale down by 10 to save cost during the ~23% zero/near-zero periods; (2) 500-50,000: queue is low relative to median (p50=108k), gently scale down by 5 to right-size capacity; (3) 50,000-200,000: around the median depth, modestly scale up by 3 to maintain processing throughput; (4) 200,000-2,000,000: above median approaching the average (~2.07M), scale up by 5 to handle growing backlog; (5) 2,000,000-10,000,000: significant backlog well above average, scale up aggressively by 10; (6) 10,000,000+: approaching p95 (~13.7M) and p99 (~16.7M) levels, maximum scale-up of 15 to handle peak load. This aligns thresholds with observed percentiles for balanced cost/latency.
rationale.strategy_impact: The balanced strategy drove selection of moderate cooldown (300s, matching the drain time which is the binding constraint), graduated step thresholds that avoid both over-provisioning during low periods and under-provisioning during peaks, and the m6a.xlarge recommendation which offers the best price-performance ratio without sacrificing capability. The scale-down steps at low queue depths ensure cost savings during the ~23% idle/low-traffic periods while the multi-tier scale-up prevents queue latency from spiraling during the heavy peak hours (UTC 19). The max_size of 150 is retained as-is since the observed peak desired_capacity reached 150.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The 300s cooldown (driven by instance_drain_seconds) means the ASG can only adjust every 5 minutes; during sudden spikes from 0 to millions of messages (which the data suggests can happen), there will be a ramp-up delay of several cooldown cycles before reaching full capacity. 2) Zero-depth percentage is 22.97%, well below the 80% threshold, so scaling to zero is not recommended and min_size should remain at 1. 3) Switching from m4.xlarge to m6a.xlarge requires validating AMI compatibility with the newer Nitro platform and AMD architecture; ensure your AMI and any CPU-specific optimizations are compatible. 4) The current max_size of 150 was hit during the analysis period, suggesting the ASG was capacity-constrained at peak; consider whether increasing max_size above 150 might improve peak latency, though this is beyond the scope of this policy recommendation. 5) The current policies have cooldown of 0/null which allows rapid successive scaling actions but risks thrashing and launching instances before previous ones are warm.
